Top-half favorites Jannik Sinner (ticks up 0.325 -> 0.330 ahead of Friday's R3 vs Jenson Brooksby) and Novak Djokovic (steady at 0.095 ahead of R3 vs Arthur Rinderknech) did not play Thursday. Top-5 sum rises to 0.755 with 0.245 on the field (Berrettini, Medvedev, Bublik, Tiafoe, FAA, Paul, Hurkacz, Fonseca, Lehecka, Dimitrov).

local_articles.title: Sinner makes net gains to book place in Wimbledon last 16, Djokovic keeps quest for 25 alive
local_articles.snippet: It was after losing in the US Open final last year that Jannik Sinner said he needed to be less predictable if he was to beat Carlos Alcaraz more regularly. Moving forward, finishing points at the net, he added, would help him against all opponents. For a while in his Wimbledon third-round encounter with Jenson Brooksby, it seemed as if Sinner had forgotten all about his own advice. With the exception of a bounce smash, he barely ventured towards the net in the first set, happy enough to crank his huge groundstrokes from the baseline instead. In the second set, though, something clicked. The Italian won 11 out of 11 points at the net and even served and volleyed four times, winning all four. Note to self: get forward. questions.current_reasoning: Significant reshuffling of the women's title contenders after Wimbledon Day 4 (July 2) and updated DraftKings odds. Defending champion Iga Swiatek [3] put her tearful R1 struggle behind her by dismantling former world No. 1 Karolina Pliskova 6-1, 6-3 in 70 minutes and enjoys the softest quarter in the draw (Q3: R3 vs Alexandra Eala [29], R4 vs Jasmine Paolini/Maria Sakkari, QF vs Marta Kostyuk/Emma Navarro/Daria Snigur/Ashlyn Krueger); surging to #3 on DraftKings (+900 title, +340 final, +160 SF), Swiatek jumps from #5 to #3 (0.075 -> 0.095). 2022 champion Elena Rybakina [2] likewise erased R1 jitters with a ruthless 6-1, 6-2 demolition of Caty McNally (+600 on DraftKings) and climbs to 0.135 (+0.015). Conversely, 2025 runner-up Amanda Anisimova [6] drops sharply (-0.030, 0.085 -> 0.055) after barely surviving world No. 105 Sofia Kenin 6-2, 4-6, 7-6(10-3) (down 1-3 in set 3, admitting 'really awful' moments) and drawing a brutal Q4 bracket (Madison Keys [26] in R3, Linda Noskova [9] R4, Rybakina QF), drifting to +1500 on DraftKings (barely holding #5 over Karolina Muchova +1500 and Coco Gauff +1600 thanks to +650 to reach final and avoiding Sabalenka until the final). Top seed Aryna Sabalenka edges up to 0.275 (+230 on DraftKings, faces Jelena Ostapenko Friday) while Jessica Pegula trims slightly to 0.075 (+1000 on DraftKings, in Sabalenka's half), leaving 0.365 on the deep field (Muchova, Gauff, Keys, Noskova, Jovic, Osaka, Kostyuk, Krejcikova, Bencic).

questions.background: India and England are scheduled to contest a T20 international series in England.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match results or contemporaneous AFP reporting identifying the winner of the England–India T20 international series in July 2026. Resolution Timing : Resolve when a team secures an unassailable series lead, or when the series concludes if its winner has not previously been determined. Accepted Answer Format : The country name of the series-winning team.
questions.current_reasoning: Two concrete June 30 squad updates on the eve of the July 1 series opener at Durham nudge this five-match series 3% back toward India (England 0.58 -> 0.55, India 0.42 -> 0.45): (1) ECB named England's playing XI for the 1st T20I (Salt, Buttler, Brook, Bethell, Banton, Curran, Jacks, Dawson, Rashid, Luke Wood, Saqib Mahmood—9 of their March 2026 T20 World Cup semifinal XI) with frontline fast bowlers Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue rested following the New Zealand Test series before rejoining for Match 2 at Old Trafford on July 4; (2) Sky Sports and IANS report mystery spinner Varun Chakravarthy—previously thought absent on June 28 and historically lethal against England's aggressive batting—has returned to India's 16-man squad for the England leg (though PTI's 15-man list omitted him). Durham's seam-friendly surface (138 avg T20I score), India's continuing absence of Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, and Suryakumar Yadav, and lingering batting vulnerability after their shock 0-2 sweep in Ireland still keep home England slight favorites (~51% Match 1 without Archer/Tongue, ~53.5% Matches 2-5 -> ~55.6% across five matches).

questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Decisive July 2 naming resolution completely bifurcates the forecast: JMA, China NMC, Taiwan CWA, HKO, and JTWC confirmed that Pacific system 09W (east of Guam) officially became Typhoon No. 9 'Bavi' at 08:00 CST July 2 (rapidly intensifying to Severe Tropical Storm at 980 hPa / 28 m/s by 20:00 CST), whereas the South China Sea depression (10W) striking Hainan July 3 and Guangxi July 4 will be Typhoon No. 10 'Maysak'. This eliminates Hainan (0.18 -> 0%) and Guangxi (0.03 -> 0%) and slashes Guangdong (0.20 -> 0.05, as HKO confirms Bavi stays well clear of the South China Sea). Bavi is unanimously forecast to rapidly intensify into a massive Cat 4/5 super typhoon (peak 58-70 m/s, 350 km gale radius) passing near Guam/Saipan Sunday July 5 and approaching China's southeast coast around July 9-11 per CMA/NMC's July 2 press briefing. Guidance splits between traditional ECMWF (stronger subtropical ridge pushing Bavi closer to northern Taiwan -> northern Fujian / southern Zhejiang) and HKO/CWA/ECMWF-AIFS (turning north through the Ryukyus into the East China Sea off Zhejiang/Shanghai). Zhejiang surges to 0.50 (+0.20) because it executes massive pre-emptive coastal/island evacuations both on direct Zhejiang/border hits and on close East China Sea near-misses (like Chan-hom 2015); Fujian rises to 0.32 (+0.07) as the prime southern/Taiwan-axis evacuator; Shanghai enters at 0.06 and Jiangsu at 0.03 for northern East China Sea tracks, leaving 0.04 tail for Shandong/other/no China evacuation by July 11.

questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Decisive July 2 naming bifurcation: WNP system 09W east of Guam was officially named Typhoon No. 9 'Bavi' at 08:00 CST July 2, while the Hainan/Guangxi-bound South China Sea system (10W) becomes Typhoon No. 10 'Maysak'. This removes Hainan (0.22 -> 0%) and Guangxi (0.04 -> 0%) and cuts Guangdong sharply (0.20 -> 0.08). Bavi is forecast to become a massive Cat 4/5 super typhoon passing near Guam/Saipan on July 5 and approaching waters east of Taiwan / China's southeast coast around July 9-11. Because this question is explicitly conditional on a qualifying mainland China landfall in July 2026 (void if Bavi recurves cleanly into Okinawa/Japan/Korea), Bayes' rule weights southward-shifted tracks (ECMWF stronger subtropical ridge pushing Bavi toward northern Taiwan -> northern Fujian / southern Zhejiang, plus central/southern Taiwan -> Fujian/Guangdong) heavily alongside East China Sea tracks bending into Zhejiang/Yangtze estuary. Zhejiang jumps to #1 at 0.42 (+0.18, intercepting both NW-angled northern-Taiwan tracks and East China Sea tracks via its eastward-protruding Zhoushan/Taizhou/Wenzhou coastline), closely followed by Fujian at 0.38 (+0.12, primary target if Bavi crosses northern/central Taiwan on a WNW heading), Guangdong at 0.08 (-0.12, southern Bashi/southern-Taiwan tail), Jiangsu at 0.045, and Shanghai at 0.04 (Yangtze-estuary/East China Sea first-landfall corridor), leaving 0.035 for Shandong/Liaoning.
